messages.subject: multinomPois error
parts:
Hi, all.  First time back to the group in 2 years after using unmarked for only a brief stint, so a little green/rusty...

I'm trying to run a multinomPois removal model for snakes on Guam:
umf<-unmarkedFrameMPois(y=y, siteCovs=scov, obsCovs=obscov, type="removal")

When I run a model, e.g.:
a12<-multinomPois(~as.numeric(min) ~vh2,   data=umf)

I get the error:
Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) : 
  initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite

In an older thread I found the suggestion that this error was sometimes the result of the new C++ handling NA's, and that "enigine="R"" should be added to the user's pcount statement.  However, when I try this with multinomPois, I get:
Error in fn(par, ...) : unused argument (engine = "R")

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] multinomPois error
parts:
Indeed, then it's not that trivial. That seems to be the latest version.

Three comments:
- that argument, "engine = R" does not exist for function multinomPois
- have you tried to supply initial values ? Try to choose them as a good guess of where the solutions might be
- Have you tried a model with intercepts only ? Often, starting with the simplest model and then using solutions from one as initial values for the next-more-complex model is a good strategy

Regards  ---  Marc
